articleTitle: A study on the integration of enterprise technological innovation and institutional innovation basing on synergetics
abstract: The relationship between the enterprise technological innovation and institutional innovation has been studied by numerous scholars, but currently, the issue of `whether the technology innovation determines the institutional innovation thereby decide the economic growth, or the institutional innovation determines the technological innovation so as to decide the economic growth' is still not solved. The author has no intention of sinking into the disputation between the `technology determinism' and the `institution determinism', but from the view of synergy that fuses enterprise technological innovation and institutional innovation to analyze the evolutionary pattern of the enterprise `technological innovation and institutional innovation' integration, and to put forward the viewpoint that the enterprise realizes sustainable development though the fusion of `technological innovation and institutional innovation'.

articleTitle: Development of innovative entrepreneurship in Croatia: Analysis and policy recommendations
abstract: The role of innovative small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the Croatian economy is comparatively smaller than in the developed European Union (EU) countries. In this paper we analyze some of the factors which contribute to such a situation, and provide some policy proposals which could address it. The proposals have been based on the analysis of current trends related to innovation activities and innovation policy. The needs and experiences of existing innovative SMEs have also been taken into account. The key recommendations include setting up an export agency, development of innovation infrastructure, employment incentives, using public procurement and EU funds for development and marketing of innovative products, adoption of the Innovation Act, development of innovative products through clusters and strengthening the linkages with the diaspora.

articleTitle: Networking scalable parallelism, integrity in knowledge economy — Civilization from shuyuans toward ubiquitous university cities
abstract: Nowadays, due to more concern on global environmental issues, establishing ecological, sustainable urbanism is widely encouraged. To promote safety-assured, mobile communication environments for engaging incorporative knowledge economy and developing contemporary growth poles, efficient, reliable maintenance and information integrity need be concerned, especially in highly possible interfered places. Regular degree-3 dedicated short range communication (DSRC) networks are suggested to support features including availability, reliability, and maintainability on detection-information services along paths of multi-lanes. Applying alternative network topologies, such as spider-webs, generalized honeycomb tori, for comparing, analyzing is proposed in fractal DSRC and cellular communications to enhance integrity in communications, and sustain flexible knowledge infrastructure for long-term economical development.

articleTitle: Management of location-based services innovation: Insights from consumers
abstract: In this project, we examine the effects of three individual-level factors - consumption values, privacy concerns, and subjective norms - on consumers' intention to adopt location-based services (LBS) on their mobile phones. A research model was created based on the Theory of Consumption Values, and tested by survey data from potential adopters. Structural equation modeling was conducted using SmartPLS. We found that consumption values positively whereas privacy concerns negatively influenced intention to adopt LBS; subjective norms were found not to impact intention. In addition, consumer intention to spread positive word-of-mouth about LBS was studied as another outcome measure. Both consumption values and subjective norms positively affected the measure, whereas privacy concerns did not. Managerial implications and theoretical contributions of the project are discussed.

articleTitle: Factors analysis on blocking knowledge creation
abstract: In the 21st, intangible resources such as knowledge and information have become important asset in an organization and consequently knowledge creation has emerged as an assure managers have to deal with. The creation and management of knowledge has become a central concern to business and management, both as a source of value and as an opportunity to achieve and sustain competitive advantage. This paper focuses on the creation of knowledge and explores how our creativity is `blocked' in a variety ways, including people's ideologies, mental factors and traditional teaching. Finally this paper takes a brief look at two ways to support knowledge creation - one is emerging individual motivation of creation and the other is to build a right climate for organization.

articleTitle: Coupling behavioral dimensions of organizational innovation in the modern workplace: A qualitative review of the literature
abstract: To take part in their potent inclination, this paper intends to explore employee engagement and OCB literatures to investigate the interrelationships between employee engagement, OCB, and organizational effectiveness. A retrospective analysis is carried out of existing theoretical and empirical research studies to support the associative interrelationship between employee engagement, OCB, and organizational effectiveness. This integrative review subsequently considers two alternative models and propositions to establish causal relationships between employee engagement, OCB, and organizational effectiveness. Findings indicate that employee engagement has potential to drive OCB. This study suggests that value-based organizations through their HR architecture should adopt high performance HR practices to sustain high levels of employee engagement, since the psychological mechanism of engagement drives OCB by which an organization achieves effectiveness. The study contributes to employee engagement and organizational effectiveness literatures by adding the notion of employee engagement as a significant antecedent of organizational effectiveness through OCB.

articleTitle: Design of environmental quality evaluation system for livestock based on feedback information
abstract: Traditional environmental quality evaluation method for livestock uses water quality, soil quality, air quality as evaluating indicators. Livestock growth character is ignored. To aim at livestock adaptability on new condition, this paper presents an environmental quality evaluation system for livestock based on feedback information, combining traditional evaluating indicators and livestock growth character. This is a new idea and of great utility value and practical significance.

articleTitle: A case study on the Chinese way of innovation
abstract: In this paper, we have used an in-depth case study of BYD to help understand the Chinese way of innovation. BYD has shown a profound understanding of local culture and market. The case analysis suggests that BYD has innovatively utilized its strategic resources and have come up with new way of production. It is also innovative in exploring its partnership networks such as adoption of a vertical integration strategy to meet the demand of ODMs. Implications for MNCs and diasporas are given at last.

articleTitle: Study on the countermeasure of innovative city construction based on science and technology innovation platform cluster
abstract: The aim of the study is to propose a new organization model of sci-tech innovation platforms for the secondary innovation resources integration to promote the development of innovative city construction, which is based on the fact that there is a positive correlation between sci-tech innovation platforms and innovative city by an empirical analysis of Fujian province.

articleTitle: Electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers' challenge: R&D strategy of battery safety units seen in WIPO data
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) is regarded as one of the most practical and effective solution for air pollution. Besides higher price and shorter cruising range, battery safety is key obstacle for its market expansion. In this thesis, analysis of corporate strategy of companies from three Asian nations by using WIPO data to show several companies will face safety restriction and have limit in procuring safe batteries.

articleTitle: Exploring the development and complements of the smart grid industry between Taiwan and China
abstract: At present, many countries devote a lot of resources to develop “smart grid”, including Taiwan and China. To establish a smart grid industry at the ground of the back-end management system, the most important subsystems are the smart meter, meter data management system, and energy information communication technology. This study mainly applied the industrial portfolio matrix composed with the industry life cycle and the industry value chain (industrial technology capability phase) to analyze the subsystem industries and its positions. Analysis results showed that the two sides have significant development in the smart meter subsystem industry, however, not in the other two, meter data management system and energy information communication technology subsystems. It proves that the two sides are still in the initial stage in the two subsystem industries.

articleTitle: Economic benefit domain of tourism area: Case study of great wall tourism area in China
abstract: A major challenge for sustainable tourism is the disparity of economic benefits for local residents. This paper provides a model of tourism areas' economic benefit domain within the framework of sustainable tourism. Field investigation by questionnaire and interview are performed in the Badaling Great Wall tourism area, a world cultural heritage site, and through which the threshold and spatial structure of sample sites' tourism benefits are analyzed according to the tourism benefit domain model. Finally, some of the theoretical and practical implications have been concluded that, the tourism managers and planners should build up different industrial strategies and community policies due to the distance-decay structure of tourism area's economic benefit domain model.

articleTitle: Management of innovation and the participation society: The case of organization learning of IBM Shenzhen Branch
abstract: This is a case study of organization learning of IBM Shenzhen Branch. Under the impact of economic convergence and globalization, governments in different nations try to promote creativity and learning behavior of their societies, including corporations. By following the “learning change model” designed by IBM Global Business Services, IBM Shenzhen Branch develops its specific organization learning with Chinese elements, with two major characteristics: an individual DIY learning plan and integration of company resources; and there are different professional learning teams, including Green Council, Lean Council, Technical Council and Delivery Council, focusing on the strategic objective of IBM. It adopts and employs a “double-loop” learning process, when errors are encountered, corrected by ways which are holistic and involve the wholesome change and modification of the organization, as well as its objectives, policies and standard procedures.

articleTitle: Research and analysis on incidence relation between technological enterprise incubator and high-end industry development
abstract: This paper starts with the development condition and character of high-end industry, and analyzes technological enterprise incubator working mechanism on high-end industry development, which based on the operating mechanism of technological enterprise incubator and the dynamic development mechanism of high-end industry. It uses incidence relation mode to do the quantitative analysis between the two terms, and comes to the conclusion that the number of the accumulated graduate incubated by technological enterprise incubator increases by every 1%, the overall industrial output of high-end will go up by 1.39%; if the total income of enterprise in the incubation increases by every 1%, it will make the overall industrial output of high-end rise by 3.12%; and the adjusted judgment factor will be up to 0.998. At the end, it makes some recommendations for the development of incubators and high-end industrial.

articleTitle: Technology innovation and new product development process integrating QFD and TRIZ
abstract: QFD (Quality Function Deployment) and TRIZ (a Russian acronym for Theory of Inventive Problem Solving) have been each one separately and thoroughly studied by authors. However, integrating both techniques QFD and TRIZ effectively for technology innovation and new product development (NPD) process remains still less explored. Using QFD and TRIZ, for new product design, is one of the best ways to meet the challenge of satisfying customers' inconstant demands and then to thrive in business. In this article we tend to describe a process which systematically integrates QFD with TRIZ and enable the effective and systematic creation of technology innovation for new products. Finally, the Balanced Scorecard (BSC) was introduced to demonstrate the practicality and efficiency of that integration.

articleTitle: New generation peasant workers employment psychological pressure and countermeasure research
abstract: In the Chinese labor market, the peasant workers employment problem is the social big problem. In recent years, new generation peasant workers replace the old, making great contribution for urban construction. Whereas, thousands of peasant workers come into city, leading to peasant workers are more than work. Employment problem make new generation peasant workers produce huge psychological pressure. This paper explores new generation peasant workers employment psychological pressure source and emotional status, building new generation peasant workers employment psychological stress model. In view of the new generation peasant workers' employment psychological pressure problems, from the government, enterprises and themselves three aspects put forward relevant policy suggestions.

articleTitle: Research on potential human capital and the regional economic growth: Based on the perspective of higher education
abstract: Human capital is the foundation of regional economy sustainable development. And the potential human capital is the basis of human capital, so the potential human capital for the development of the region economy also has positive influence. The article, based on the number of college graduates as the proxy variable, verifies the effect that the potential human capital on regional economic growth. And put forward the suggestion that backward areas can narrow the economic disparity which compared with developed area through improving the level of human capital.

articleTitle: Keynote speakers
abstract: Dr. Annalee Saxenian is Professor and Dean at the U.C. Berkeley School of Information and a Professor in Berkeley's department of city and regional planning. She has made a career of studying regional economics and the conditions under which people, ideas, and geographies combine and connect into hubs of economic activity. Her latest book, The New Argonauts: Regional Advantage in a Global Economy (Harvard University Press, 2006) explores how and why immigrant engineers from Silicon Valley have transferred the institutions of technology entrepreneurship to emerging regions in their home countries-Taiwan, Israel, China and India in particular-and launching companies far from established centers of skill and technology. The ℌbrain drain,ℍ she argues, has now become ℌbrain circulationℍ — a powerful economic force for the development of formerly peripheral regions that is sparking profound transformations in the global economy.

articleTitle: Variable selection for international bankruptcy forecasts
abstract: Corporate financial distress not only incurs serious financial loss to its creditors but also has a high cost to the society and the country's economy. Consequently, financial distress prediction studies are important to all those involved: owners, shareholders, lenders, suppliers, and government. In this paper, we focus on the corporate bankruptcy prediction for international market using CompuStat Global database. First, we introduce a robust variable selection technique, called adaptive lasso (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator), on the global corporate bankruptcy data in search for a parsimonious default forecasting model. Second, we demonstrate a comprehensive case study on Japan bankruptcy prediction. Comparing to US and UK, significant variables selected are generally different across countries. Only firm's activity indicator Sales/Total Assets displays uniform significance across three countries.

articleTitle: Integration and innovation of the government-sponsored sci-tech financial resource: Experience from the SIP
abstract: This article analyses the successes and problems of the sci-tech finance in the Suzhou Industrial Park (SIP), and proposes strategies for the government-sponsored sci-tech financial resource. It is suggested that the sci-tech bank should provide industry-specialized financial services, the venture capital should be integrated with the business incubators, the small-sum loan company should find more flexible source of fund, and the government should help the financial institutions with sci-techappraisalby the public intelligence.

articleTitle: Research on the technical efficiency and influences of China's cultural industry listed companies
abstract: Data envelopment analysis (DEA) approach was applied in this paper to measure technical efficiencies of China's cultural industry listed companies. Efficiency influence factors were evaluated through our econometric models. The results indicate that technical efficiencies of China's cultural industry listed companies are not high, only 52.4% is technical efficient, and 28.6% is scale efficient. Among the cultural industry listed companies, the technical efficiencies of film and television companies are higher than advertisement companies and publications companies. The technical efficiencies of GEM board listed companies are higher than main board listed companies and small and medium-sized board listed companies. The regression analysis on efficiency influence factors shows that technology innovation ability has obvious positive effect on technical efficiency and is significant at 10% level, human resource has positive effect on technical efficiency but is not significant.

articleTitle: Study on enterprises' independent innovation mode from the perspective of resource integration — A case study of GONA Technology Co., Ltd.
abstract: This paper, based on the development history of Dalian GONA technology Co., Ltd., investigates enterprises' independent innovation mode established by integrating internal and external resources in face of changing demand and continuous competition. It finds that the core of enterprises' independent innovation lies in the integration of internal and external resources, and mode is the integral network innovation through group aggregation and chain integration.

articleTitle: Entrepreneurship of overseas Chinese businessmen in post-financial crisis era: Two case studies of Chinese businessman in Japan and Korea
abstract: More and more attention is paid to the interactive development between the economic integration of China-Japan-Korea and the economy of overseas Chinese. By analyzing the business cases about Japanese and Korean Chinese Businessman Song Wenzhou, Xue Rongxing, we find that Japanese and Korean Chinese businessmen are forced to venture and start from scratch; with higher education they are quite sharp to market opportunities; actively integrate into the society and transform in a timely manner; promote investment to China and boost the economic cooperation between China, Japan and Korea. Providing an institutional and policy support for Chinese businessmen in Japan and Korea will propel the development of them and the process of economic integration of China-Japan-Korea.

articleTitle: Profitability of pairs trading tactics in China's stock market
abstract: On the hypothesis of short selling being possible in Shanghai stock market, using standardized stock price series, selecting sample based on the constituent stocks of SSE 50 index, this paper tests the profitability of pairs trading tactics. By use of constructing benchmark and bootstrap simulation, this paper demonstrates that pairs trading tactics is profitable in Chinese securities market. The system risk of this tactics is close to zero, which reflects the pairs trading tactics being a market neutral tactics.

articleTitle: The study for microscopic location of multinational R&D institutions in China: A case study of Suzhou Industrial Park
abstract: Based on the neoclassical microeconomic location theory, the paper studies the spatial layout of multinational corporations in China, and takes Suzhou Industrial Park as an empirical case. Suzhou Industrial Park has been in the development of export-oriented economy since 1994, industry-embedded by the government's economic promotion. By using GIS space analysis technology, this paper concludes that the micro layout of multinational R&D institutions tends to layout in the following three types of location: the large multinational companies, the industry gathering areas, and the centralized innovation parks (planned by the government). The spatial pattern gradually forms a “point - axis - area” evolution model. Finally, the article points out that by planning scientific and technological innovation park, making out of science and technology policies, local government can play a key role in creating regional innovation atmosphere, and attracting the R&D institutions to settle.

articleTitle: Research on American small and medium-sized business innovation entrepreneurship policy and reference to China
abstract: Due to the double pressures of the global economic crisis and rising costs, small and medium-sized enterprise's survival and development face new challenges. The small business in the United States has high informatization level, which is not only the important force of technology innovation, but also has wide social connections, especially with big businesses. Reasons should be attributed to the implementation of a series of polices and laws, including setting up special service agencies, providing funding, training, information consultation, and other supporting measures. In this paper, by analyzing the quo of small businesses in the United States, summarizing the policies and measures of the United States in promoting the development of small businesses, our country gains references in promoting small and medium-sized enterprise innovation entrepreneurship development, including forming service system and financial support. Maybe these things will rely on the government, but the most important thing is to build up the healthy and benign environment for small and medium-sized enterprise, ensuring the development of enterprises.

articleTitle: China's way towards innovation and competition: The perspective of intellectual property
abstract: The purpose of this study is to offer a snapshot of the evolution of innovation in China from the angle of the intellectual property policy initiatives. Based on a detailed investigation in the intellectual property sector, it also tries to reveal the dilemma in China's intellectual property pushing innovation, and whether China has succeeded in forming a synergistic relationship between technology policy and intellectual property system. It argues that China, as a huge and fast-going emerging economy, needs to rethink its innovation and intellectual property Policy in based on a long-term strategic consideration.

articleTitle: Green policies and green businesses
abstract: The business environment becomes increasingly competitive. More and more companies are cautious about their environmental performance and willing to fulfill their social responsibilities. In this paper, we propose taxonomy of green policies that are particularly relevant and explicitly targeted at corporate greenhouse gases emissions reduction. The taxonomy includes environmental taxes, tradable emissions permits, conventional taxes, and voluntary approaches. We identified environmental labels as good ways for companies to reveal how green their products are. And we developed an analytical model to explore the relationship between environmental label and company profit.

articleTitle: Organizational entrepreneurial climate and entrepreneurial orientation: The role of entrepreneurial self-efficacy
abstract: Based on social cognitional theory, this study proposes an organizational entrepreneurial climate based model of entrepreneurial orientation. The model indicates the complex interaction among organizational entrepreneurial climate(OEC), entrepreneurial self-efficacy(ESE) and entrepreneurial orientation(EO). The empirical study results show that the model has a good fit. OEC has a significant effect on EO. Also, a mediating effect of ESE on the relationship between OEC and EO is identified.

articleTitle: Influential factors and area differentiation of carbon emissions for agriculture in China
abstract: Based on Carbon Emissions for agriculture in China, we appraise the area differentiation of Carbon Emissions for agriculture; examine the influential factors of carbon emissions for agriculture in China. The results show that the whole country's agricultural carbon emissions performance is on the rise. The carbon emissions for agriculture in west increase rapidly. The area differentiation of Carbon Emissions for agriculture in China decreases. In general, the major driver of carbon emissions was agricultural development level. Industrial structure energy efficiency and labor transfer have significant effects on agricultural carbon emissions performance.

articleTitle: The internationalization process of born global high technology SMEs: The moderating role of business and social networks
abstract: This paper examines the moderating role of business and social networks in the internationalization process of born global high technology Small and Medium Sized Enterprises (SMEs) in the context of developed and emerging economies. We develop a conceptual model in which the relationship between the two types of networks and the internationalization process (speed, geographic scope and entry mode) is analysed. We conclude that both business and social networks contribute to faster internationalization and offer necessary knowledge on new market opportunities. Our model aligns with previous studies and depicts the important role that institutional networks, part of business networks in this study, play in the internationalization process. We suggest that policy makers and entrepreneurs of high technology SMEs should be encouraged to develop all the necessary mechanisms to support and enhance early internationalization.

articleTitle: Learning from experience: Novice and serial immigrant entrepreneurs in Silicon Valley
abstract: Despite theoretical arguments for distinguishing between novice and serial entrepreneurs, empirical evidence on their differences remains inconclusive. This paper extends existing research, using a unique dataset of primarily immigrant Silicon Valley entrepreneurs. It finds that serial entrepreneurs displayed higher aspirations, embedded and diverse social networks, reliance on collaborators, access to external finance, and better performance, compared with novice entrepreneurs. Novices performed better with greater access to social capital and when collaborating with co-founders and advisors. Serial entrepreneurs reported higher performance when working alone. These findings contribute toward advancing our understanding of the value of experience on entrepreneurship, with theoretical and practical implications.

articleTitle: The historical evolution and coordination status of the policies on National Economic and Technological Development Zones in China
abstract: Policies play a crucial role in the development of National Economic and Technological Development Zones (NETDZs) in China. This paper scans the NETDZ policies in China from number distributions, departments involved and instruments, and studies policies' continuities, complementarities, absences and crosses. We conclude that: The main contents of NETDZ policies have evolved from initially offering preferential policies, to regulating the development, and to now improving the development level; The NETDZ policies show good continuities and complementarities, but there are policy absences and crosses.

Author Keywords: National Economic and Technological Development Zones

articleTitle: Analyze the business service models of electric vehicles (EV) based batteries
abstract: This research mainly applied innovation intensive service matrix as basic structure to set up position analysis of the electric vehicles (EV) based batteries service industry. It inducts the positions of four EV based batteries service models, which leading by different type manufacturers, per the viewpoints from EV manufactures, EV based batteries manufacturers and R&D institutes. It analyzes, and then conducts the approach to cut to EV batteries industry service model, and finds out the critical success factors of EV batteries industry, and finally provides future administration strategies of service models. The results of the studies indicates: Service Model A moves from unique package structure of product innovation at present to unique package structure of structure innovation in future; Service Model B moves from unique package structure of product innovation at present to restricted package structure of structure innovation in future; Service Model C moves from unique package structure of structure innovation at present to generic package structure of market innovation in future; Service Model D moves from restricted package structure of process innovation at present to generic package structure of market innovation in future.

articleTitle: Jumping over latecomers' upgrading barriers: The exploration of China's upgrading opportunities by Taiwan's machine tool industry
abstract: Most existing studies of late industrialization emphasize that latecomers' successful catch-up were driven by the learning mechanisms embedded in their linkages with advanced firms and regions in industrialized countries. It is through such linkages the latecomers were able to source critical technological knowledge and market information for further upgrading and higher competitiveness. This paper argues that such literature neglects to consider the possibilities that latecomers could also obtain learning and upgrading capabilities through their linkages with other late industrializing counterparts. By using the investments of Taiwan's machine tool (MT) industry in China as the example, this paper analyzes how Taiwanese MT firms advanced their technological capabilities through exploring and exploiting China's technological and market resources. More specifically, it discusses the significance of China in enabling Taiwanese industrial firms to acquire complementary knowledge and skills that have been not available in their existing business and relational networks.

Author Keywords: technological learning catch-up machine tool industry

articleTitle: A case study: Innovation strategy assessment of the leading smartphone companies
abstract: Using our Enterprise Innovation Index framework, we have analyzed innovation strategy for four leading smartphone companies - Apple, Samsung, Nokia and Xiaomi, and generated a scorecard. Our scorecard for the innovation strategy assessment is well supported by smartphone market data. Samsung, Apple and Xiaomi are market leaders in different market segments, i.e. mass market, high-end and middle-end respectively, which are driven by their innovation strategies. Coming back from near-death experience, Nokia's growth will strongly depend on grabbing the opportunity of disruptive innovation. To achieve sustainable future growth, smartphone makers really need to think about the best innovation strategies to establish market leadership.

articleTitle: University science parks and promoting knowledge transfer in emerging economies: A study on required attributes with evidences from South Africa and China
abstract: As a challenge to traditional theories, some university science parks (USPs) in emerging countries appear to show their capabilities in knowledge transfer recently. This paper, therefore, aims to explore the attributes that are required for these USPs in emerging countries to better promote knowledge transfer. This paper develops an analytical framework through analyzing two selected cases in South Africa and China from an open innovation perspective, and required attributes are classified as link building for knowledge exploration and knowledge commercialization for exploitation. On institutional level, property right policy, support from government, and proper rules of academic appraisal are found to be key attributes, while tenant service and management of park-university partnership are salient ones on park-level. This paper originally explores the knowledge-transfer of USPs in two important emerging economies, South Africa and China. It will be of great interest to policy makers, academic researchers, investors, and entrepreneurs.

articleTitle: Migrating birds: Why transnational bioscience entrepreneurs return home
abstract: Transnational bioscience entrepreneurs (TBEs) accelerate not only the economic, but also the cultural, political, and social development of their host and sending countries. Today, the ease with which TBEs shuttle between American, Chinese, and Taiwanese cultures and resolve intractable workplace norms such as haphazard research, inadequate quality control, insular attitudes, and misguided regulations throws into sharp relief the significance of the TBEs' global sensibility. This paper uses grounded theory building to understand how intellectual engagement and rootedness are precursors to global sensibility. Analyzing the experiences and motivations of TBEs advances our understanding of why they return to their country of origin to upgrade its bioscience infrastructure.

articleTitle: Interaction effects on concentration of entrepreneurial behaviors — Perspective of initial conditions in new venture creation
abstract: This paper examines interaction effects on concentration of entrepreneurial behaviors based on perspective of initial conditions in new venture creation. We put forward theoretical model according to entrepreneurial learning, and test these hypotheses using longitudinal data from Chinese Panel Study of Entrepreneurial Dynamics. Concentration is influenced by appropriate matching of key factors including prior experience, entrepreneurial opportunity and learning strategy. (1) interaction of prior start-up experience and newness of market; (2) interaction of prior industry experience and product innovation; (3) interaction of prior start-up experience and incremental learning strategy; (4) interaction of product innovation and incremental learning strategy are negatively related to the concentration. This paper concludes with some suggestions for the role of entrepreneurial learning for furthering insights into the process of new venture creation.

articleTitle: Research on sino-foreign technology learning and competition game in catch-up stage: Case study of large-scale wind power equipment manufacture industry in China
abstract: The progress of developing country industry's technological catch-up is multi-stage game among catch-up enterprises, leading enterprises and the government of developing country. The process of game is divided into two consecutive phases of “learning in a group” and “completing in a group”, as well as “deep learning” and “multiple completing”. Through constructing game models and analyzing evolution progress of large-scale wind power equipment manufacture industry in China, it reveals under the guidance of the government's industrial policy about leading enterprises and catch-up enterprises how to select each action tactics based on the technical gap, the learning speed of catch-up enterprises, market opportunities. Meanwhile, it also shows the Government's action tactics about how to adjust industrial policy timely according to the transfer will of leading companies and the technologic alliance between the leading enterprises.

articleTitle: The current state of valuating early stage technologies: Anecdotal evidences and a new conceptual model
abstract: Early technology valuation has been a critical element in the process of technology commercialization. Current methods have been overly theoretical in methodology, and an aggregated view is yet to be witnessed. In this research, a series of field interviews and existing literature provided guidance for us to develop a technology valuation framework that comprehensively integrated quantitative and qualitative techniques for the valuation of early stage technologies. A heuristic method is also developed to implement necessary computational methods. Due to the page limit for conference submission, the computational method is not included here and it is available upon request.

articleTitle: How do the top Chinese returnee entrepreneurs innovate?
abstract: Chinese government at different levels has elevated the competition for global talents to a strategic level. Against such a background, this paper presents a number of interesting findings on the basis of a study of three start-ups founded by Chinese returnees under the Recruitment Program of Global Experts plan: 1) The Chinese government has given preferences to returnees who start up businesses in the 7 strategic industries designated by the Chinese government; 2) Top-level returnee entrepreneurs prefer to select high potential opportunities positioning on global markets, while the domestic markets for such high tech products are yet to develop; and 3) Top-level returnee entrepreneurs tend to skip the product imitation stage, and directly engage in original technology and product development.

articleTitle: Metropolitan innovation mode: A case study of New York
abstract: People are already familiar with stories about innovation in Silicon Valley. It presents a specialized innovation mode, which is based on universities of science and technology. However, people pay little attention to another high-tech innovation center-New York. This paper points out that unlike Silicon Valley which has strong science and technology universities like Stanford and Berkeley, New York presents a unique innovation mode. New York possesses a metropolitan platform with diversified resources and has the advantages of agglomeration effect and being close to market demand. This paper systematically analyses the industrial structure, universities, government, social networks, and HR and entrepreneurship of New York, and how these five aspects promote innovation. In the context of 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> century industrial revolution, the revitalization of metropolitan innovation mode, New York as an example, is a new trend worthy further study.

articleTitle: How public demonstration project affects the emergence of a new industry: An empirical study on electric vehicle demonstration project in China
abstract: Public demonstration projects are receiving increasing attention, especially when some developing economies attempt to accelerate the emergence of new industries - though being questioned - through government interventions. This paper, therefore, aims to explore whether these demonstration policies can promote industrial emergence, at least in China; and what is the influential mechanism behind? This paper investigates China's demonstration project on electrical vehicle - “Ten Cities Thousand Cars” programme - through a survey with 1500 questionnaires. 437 valid returns have been analyzed by using the structural equation modeling (SEM) method. The result shows that the public demonstration project is effective in terms of information, application, and product diffusion. In addition, the result also validates the model that illustrates how demonstration policies affect industrial innovation via testing and showing functions. This paper helps to better understand how demonstration policies intervene industrial emergence, and it will be of interest to policy makers, industrialists and academics.

articleTitle: Research on IP strategy on the frame of open-innovation: Case study in France and China
abstract: Innovation is getting increasingly crucial for a company to maintain its comparative advantage and remain leadership in the market. The concept of open innovation indicates that firms can boost their innovative performance by both acquiring knowledge from outside the company and employing external paths to market for commercialization of key technologies. Current researches on open innovation application in China are still unclear and immature. Through a series of data description and comparative analysis, the research explored the open innovation mechanism and its outcomes by comparing five sample enterprises from China and France. Their organizational structure and intellectual property issues are specially discussed in the paper. The conclusion is instructive for China, which suggest that both the government and the enterprises should change their relatively conservative idea and take action to adopt the open innovation strategy.

articleTitle: The determinants of China's inter-provincial R&D intensity: Evidence from the dynamic panel models of interprovincial data
abstract: Since investments in R&D have been identified as a major engine of growth by the proponents of the endogenous growth models, many studies have investigated the determinants of R&D intensity. In this study, our primary objective is to establish, empirically, the determinants of inter-provincial R&D intensity in China over the period 2001 to 2010. We collected both cross-sectional and time series data for 31 provinces, municipalities, and autonomous regions of China and the estimation of our model was done using the fixed effect model, random effect model, Difference GMM, and System GMM. Our findings reveal that factors such as economic development level, investment in science and technology, and human capital have a significant positive effect on R&D Intensity, but trade openness has a negative and significant impact on R&D intensity. Even though the fixed asset investment has a negative relationship with R&D intensity, it is not statistically significant.

articleTitle: The effect of external linkage on hub-spoke industrial cluster
abstract: Although industrial cluster attracts great attention, it still holds some research deficiencies. Rare exploration about cluster's external linkage is the most significant one. To make up such deficiency, this paper takes hub-spoke industrial cluster as example to analyze the influence and effect path of external linkage on cluster. Finally for more information about external linkage's effects, this paper identifies the order of different external linkage forms with ZhongGuanCun(ZGC) as research object and further analyzes the reason of the final quantitive result.

articleTitle: A game theoretical approach to the co-optition between the core enterprise and general partner among the technological alliance
abstract: There are some different traits about the collaborative technological innovation between the core enterprise and general partner among the technological alliance. Based on the Ngo et al (2008), this paper analyzes the innovation cost, the competition level and the co-opetitive relationships from Stackelberg game theoretical approach, and comes to the following conclusions: when the core enterprise competes first, the higher the social responsibility, the less the competitive effort for the core enterprise, and the more the competitive effort for the general partner, and vice versa. When the core enterprise competes first, the competitive effort and social responsibility are substitutes for general partner, while the relationship between the competitive effort and social responsibility depends on social responsibility for core firm. As far as co-opetition concerned, the relationship between the competitive and cooperative effort level are mediated by the social responsibility.

articleTitle: Analysis on innovation environment factors in high-tech enterprises of Poyang Lake ecological economic zone
abstract: High technology enterprise on the process of independent innovation will be affected by the environment of policies, legal, market, resources, social service, science and technology, as well as social culture environment. Using the structural equation model methods to analyze 217 high technology enterprises of ecological economic zone in Poyang Lake, and then to verify a fact that these environments are important factors for independent innovation of High-tech enterprises. Also find that the environment of social services, science and technology contribute the biggest, their contribution rate is more than 0.9; next factors are the market environment and the social cultural environment, theirs is between 0.8 and 0.9; finally, policies and legal environment and resources environment contribute less than 0.7.

articleTitle: A dominant retailer's optimal pricing strategy to stimulate upstream innovation
abstract: Consider a basic two-echelon retailer-Stackelberg supply chain in which the supplier sells a product to a retailer, who in turns retails it to the consumers. The supplier has the opportunity to invest in process innovation to reduce his marginal production cost. However, due to the existence of the classical “double marginalization” and “hold-up” problems, the supplier will tend to invest less than what would be optimal from the perspective of the whole supply chain. The question we pose is: how to stimulate the supplier's innovation via appropriately designed contract format from the dominant retailer's perspective. We examined the performance of two contract formats (namely, markup-only commitment contract, and markup commitment with lump-sum payment contract) and our results show that, markup commitment with lump-sum payment contract always dominants the markup-only commitment contract, not only because it can effectively stimulate the supplier's innovation investment, but also it can full coordinate the supply chain.

articleTitle: Sustainability in supply chain management how to execute the triple bottom line
abstract: We will discuss the execution of sustainability in supply chain management. Firms need effective leadership to establish the vision of sustainability but the critical issue we've found in our work is execution. Therefore we discuss the following topics in relation to execution and conclude with a brief case study of the Sonoma Wine Company: situational stakeholder management, the role of NGOs, socially responsible investing and its influence on the firm, and cooperative competition in establishing environmental standards. With reference to the case study, we discuss many fronts along which sustainability management is executed in an integrated fashion.

articleTitle: Study on relationship between network embeddedness and innovation performance in China
abstract: With the development of economic globalization, FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) has been clustering in China. The study on how FDI's spillover improving innovation capability in local firms by network embeddedness has become a hot topic in the academic and business circles. Integrating network embeddedness, knowledge acquisition, absorptive capacity with innovation performance, this paper is to explain how network embeddedness affects innovation performance by knowledge acquisition for local firms. By building a conceptual model and empirical analysis, it shows that network embeddedness can improve innovation performance by knowledge spillover during FDI clustering, and absorptive capacity plays the intermediary role between them. Furthermore, it provides some theoretical guidelines and suggestions for local firms to improve their innovation capability.

articleTitle: Research on coevolution and upgrading of talent flow and regional advantage of late-development — A case study of Dalian High-tech Zone, China
abstract: Talent aggregation in a particular region - as a result of talent flow - plays a significant role in promoting regional advantages. For developing countries, it is a gradual process to bring the regional advantage of late-development (RAL) into full play through enhancing regional talent competitiveness (RTC). Based on a case study of Dalian High-tech Zone, China, this study elaborates upon the coevolution between talent flow and RAL, the contribution of enhanced RTC to the improvement of RAL, from the following 4 aspects: talent attraction, talent fostering, talent deployment, and talent development; and it also points out that the factors contributing to RTC, as well as the internal mechanism of promoting the upgrading of RAL, bear features different from those arising from existing findings.
